title: Fallback Transparency & Customer Communication Playbook
author: Daniel H. Park
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook describes the recommended approach for transparent, consistent communication with customers when Redwood serves a fallback model, reduced-fidelity response, or routes to alternative capacity tiers. The goal is to preserve trust and predictable billing behavior while meeting SLOs and protecting customer experience.

Scope
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments where automatic or policy-driven fallback may occur.
- Covers runtime triggers, customer-facing messaging, telemetry we expose, and the incident/rollback procedimento for staged rollouts.
- Does not replace legal/contracting language; coordinate with Sales and Legal for contractual changes.

Intended audience
Product managers, customer success, support engineering, oncall SRE, and growth/account teams.

Principles
- Be proactive: customers should receive clear, machine-readable signals and human-friendly notices when fidelity or model selection changes impact their requests.
- Preserve user experience: prefer silent, behind-the-scenes fallbacks when degradation is below target thresholds; escalate to notifications when measurable customer impact occurs.
- Make billing transparent: any fallback that materially changes cost or quota consumption must be visible in Console and API telemetry.

Service-level triggers and classification
1) Transparent fallback (info-only):
   - Trigger: runtime selects a compatible lower-cost model variant with equal API contract but potentially different output characteristics.
   - SLO impact: no measurable latency/regression beyond 5% of baseline.
   - Action: Emit telemetry and mark requests with header X-Redwood-Fallback: variant=low-cost-info. No proactive email.

2) Fidelity degradation (noticeable):
   - Trigger: quantization or variant selection that reduces measured quality against tenant gold prompts (regression > 3% NIST-style metric or >5% human eval delta).
   - SLO impact: output-fidelity SLO may be in degraded state.
   - Action: Send Console banner + email to billing contact. Provide advice and rollback link (see Rollback steps).

3) Capacity failover (customer-visible slowdown or routing):
   - Trigger: regional capacity shortage causes routing to different region or preemptible capacity leading to >30% latency increase or >10% token cost delta.
   - SLO impact: latency and cost SLOs may be violated.
   - Action: Outbound incident page update, in-console banner, and optional scheduled call for enterprise tenants.

Ownership matrix
- Detection & Runtime signal: Eng - Serving Runtime (owner: runtime-alerts@redwood.com)
- Customer messaging templates: Product (owner: product-commissions@redwood.com)
- Billing & telemetry exposure: Finance + Eng Platform (owner: billing-data@redwood.com)
- Oncall escalation & postmortem: Eng SRE (owner: oncall@redwood.com)

Customer-facing channels and message taxonomy
- Console banner: short, contextual, includes action link (View details, Rollback, Explain impact).
- Email/Account notification: reserved for notice-level or above; templates include severity, expected duration, mitigation, and contact steps.
- Status page: incident-level only.
- API response headers: include X-Redwood-Fallback and X-Redwood-Fidelity-Risk with machine-readable codes.

Message templates (copy-ready)
1) Console banner (informational)
- Title: "Variant selection notice: performance optimization applied"
- Body: "We served an optimized model variant for some requests to improve latency/cost. Outputs remain compatible; if you notice changes, use 'View details' to compare.
  Action: [View details] [Request rollback]"

2) Email (notice-level)
- Subject: "Notice: Temporary fidelity change for <tenant-name> on Redwood"
- Body: "Hi <contact>,

We applied a temporary fidelity optimization for some requests associated with your account to maintain latency SLOs in the region. Expected impact: small changes to output quality for certain prompts. If this is unacceptable, click 'Request rollback' or contact your AEs. We expect to revert within <estimated-duration>.

Summary of action items: 
- How to opt out: Console > Settings > Fallback Policies.
- How to request support: support@redwood.com (Priority: enterprise + SSO links).

Regards,
Redwood Inference Product Team"

3) Status page (incident) excerpt
- Title: "Regional failover: some requests routed to preemptible capacity"
- Body: "We are routing traffic from <region> to alternative capacity due to a GPU pool disruption. We are monitoring and expect stabilization within 2 hours. See console for affected tenants."

Rollout and rollback procedures (numbered)
1. Detection: Runtime emits fallback event with payload (tenant_id, route, fallback_code, reason, sample_request_id).
2. Automated triage: Playbook-runner queries golden prompt registry (golden-sets/<tenant_id>) to run a quick fidelity check (5 representative prompts).
3. Classification: If regression < threshold_1 (see thresholds table), mark as transient; if >= threshold_1 escalate to Notice.
4. Notification: For Notice/Incident classes, trigger Console banner and email for Notice; status page and CC to customer success for Incident.
5. Mitigation options:
   a) Automatic: If the fallback was due to transient capacity and completes within 10 minutes, mark as auto-resolved and send optional digest.
   b) Manual rollback: Support or tenant can perform variant roll-forward/rollback via Console API: POST /v1/tenants/{id}/fallbacks?action=rollback with body {"fallback_event_id": "..."}.
6. Post-event review: SRE owns 72-hour incident review for Incident-level events and completes a lightweight RCA and a customer impact summary.

Thresholds and SLO mapping (table representation)
- threshold_1: fidelity_regression_pct = 3
- threshold_2: fidelity_regression_pct = 10
- latency_increase_pct_notice = 15
- latency_increase_pct_incident = 30
- cost_delta_pct_notice = 10
- cost_delta_pct_incident = 30

Map to SLOs
- If fidelity_regression_pct >= threshold_1 AND measured across >1% of tenant traffic -> Notice
- If latency_increase_pct >= latency_increase_pct_incident for >5 minutes -> Incident

Telemetry and Console changes (configuration table)
- Exposed metrics (Console): fallback.rate, fallback.by_variant, fallback.regression_pct, fallback.latency_delta_pct, fallback.cost_delta_pct
- Logs: structured event with keys: tenant_id, event_id, fallback_code, fallback_variant, sample_prompt_hash, evaluated_metrics
- Console UX additions: "Fallback history" tab under Tenant > Activity showing events, quick A/B diff tool for sample responses, and one-click rollback.

Example runtime event (JSON snippet)
{
  "event_id": "fb-20261129-01",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-123",
  "fallback_code": "VARIANT_LOW_CPU",
  "variant": "mova-quant-8",
  "detected_at": "2026-11-29T10:12:30Z",
  "regression_metrics": { "auto_eval_f1": "0.86->0.81" }
}

API header contract
- X-Redwood-Fallback: code=VARIANT_LOW_CPU;variant=mova-quant-8
- X-Redwood-Fidelity-Risk: score=0.12 (decimal 0..1 where >0.1 is noticeable)

Console UX flows (short)
- Tenant > Activity > Fallback history: list sorted by time, filterable by code and severity.
- Fallback detail view: side-by-side diff of 3 sample responses (before/after), ranked by consumer impact score.
- Rollback: button that opens modal with risk checklist; requires owner_team confirmation for enterprise tenants.

Billing considerations
- Whenever a fallback event changes per-token cost by >cost_delta_pct_notice, the Console must show an estimated cost delta for the billing period and include an "Adjust Pricing" link to engage Account Team.
- For any billed preemptible capacity use, we surface a line-item in the billing export named "fallback_preemptible_tokens".

Operational runbook (short checklist)
- Oncall receives an alert: check fallback.rate and fallback.regression_pct dashboards.
- Run automated golden-set sample check (playbook-runner).
- If Incident: trigger status page, inform Sales/CS, and start RCA.
- If Notice: inform customer via Console banner + email, run A/B samples, and offer rollback.

Guidance for Sales & Customer Success
- For Enterprise customers: proactively schedule a 30-minute sync for any Incident-level fallback. Provide a summary of triggers, affected routes, and remediation plan.
- For SMB customers: use templated email and link to self-serve rollback where applicable.

Metrics to track (30/60/90 day cadence)
- % of tenants that experience at least one Notice-level fallback per month
- Mean time to auto-resolve fallback events
- % of rollbacks requested by customers vs. auto-resolved
- Customer satisfaction delta (CSAT) for customers exposed to rollback events

Open decisions (for product & eng)
- Whether automatic rollback should be allowed for enterprise tenants without a human in the loop. (Owner: Product - decision due 2027-01-15)
- Define the consumer-impact-score algorithm and what weight gold prompts receive vs. real traffic. (Owner: Eng Applied ML - decision due 2027-02-01)

Related links
- Golden prompt registry (internal): /tools/golden-prompts/
- Fallback event schema (design-spec): /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/fallback-event-schema
- Billing export schema: /confluence/finance-and-legal/billing/billing-export-schema

Appendix: example console rollback API call
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/tenant-123/fallbacks?action=rollback" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"fallback_event_id":"fb-20261129-01","reason":"customer_request"}'

Appendix: short FAQ
Q: Will customer requests for rollback cause additional charges?
A: Rollback itself does not incur extra token charges; however, if rollback routes to higher-cost variants, expected cost-per-token will change and be visible in Console.

Q: How do we calculate the fidelity_regression_pct?
A: Primary method: automated golden-set scoring using normalized f1 and BLEU variants; also augmented with production-sampled human evaluations for tenants on enterprise plans.

Q: Who gets notified for private deployments?
A: For private (VPC/on-prem) customers, the local admin contact is the default notification recipient; Redwood will also notify the assigned TAM and account team.

End of document
